title: Director, AI Governance & Risk
description: JOB SUMMARY: The Office of General Counsel is responsible for overseeing all elements of the Firm's privacy compliance program. This program includes the Firm's privacy policies, notices, records of processing, impact assessments, transfer agreements, data processing agreements, data subject access requests and all other matters related to complying with applicable privacy and data security laws. The Director, AI Governance & Risk will play a key role in maturing, implementing, and overseeing Simpson Thacher’s AI governance framework, policies and controls to ensure responsible, ethical, secure and compliant use of artificial intelligence. This role will report to the Chief Risk Officer and will be part of a multi-disciplinary team focused on accelerating the adoption of appropriate AI tools and technologies across the Firm. The Director will bridge legal, risk, compliance, technology & business teams to manage AI-related risks across the full AI lifecycle – from ideation and development to deployment and monitoring. As a senior leader , t he Director will lead Firm-wide AI governance initiatives, align AI practices with regulatory requirements and industry standards, and serve as a key advisor to Partners and Senior Leadership on AI risk, ethics and controls. JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: Develop, implement and maintain the Firm’s AI governance framework, including policies, standards, controls and operation procedures Establish governance processes for evaluating AI use cases, the selection of appropriate tools and technologies, assessing technology developments and vendor due diligence Ensure data and information governance aligns, enables and supports the adoption of AI tools and technologies Support the development and enhancement of AI user capability across the Firm, including the development of appropriate training for lawyers, professional staff and leaders Identify, assess and mitigate AI-related risks, including data privacy, cybersecurity, and third party/vendor risk Partner with the Office of General Counsel, Information Security, Information Governance and Knowledge & Innovation teams to integrate AI risks in existing risk frameworks Monitor and interpret global AI-related regulation standards and ensure AI systems and practices comply with applicable laws, regulations and internal policies Advise the Firm in relation to responsible AI principles and ethical guidelines Serve as a trusted advisor to Partners and Senior Leadership on AI risk and governance matters Drive AI governance awareness and training across the Firm Promote a culture of responsible AI use and accountability EDUCATION: JD required SKILLS & EXPERIENCE: Qualified lawyer, with 6-10 years of practicing experience at an international law firm Minimum 2-5 years of relevant experience in AI, risk and compliance Strategic thinking with strong execution capability Regulatory interpretation and policy development Demonstrated experience supporting and executing large-scale, firm-wide projects Cross-functional leadership and excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to influence the actions of internal stakeholders and manage relationships with external stakeholders Broad knowledge of information management and protection laws, regulations, and best practices Ability to balance innovation with risk management POSTING DISCLOSURE: Simpson Thacher will not sponsor applicants for work visas for this position. Salary Information NY Only: The estimated base salary range for this position is $325,000 to $375,000 at the time of posting. The actual salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including without limitation, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and if applicable, the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. This role is exempt meaning it is not overtime pay eligible. Simpson Thacher will not sponsor applicants for work visas for this position. title: Associate General Counsel, Product Regulatory
description: CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at  www.coreweave.com . What You’ll Do: The Legal and Government Affairs team at CoreWeave is highly collaborative and partners closely with teams across the company to navigate complex legal landscapes while enabling innovation and growth. The team is pragmatic, solutions-oriented, and deeply engaged in strategic decision-making, with a strong emphasis on building trusted relationships across the organization. As Associate General Counsel, Product Regulatory , you will play a critical role in shaping how CoreWeave develops, launches, and scales its products as our business and the regulatory landscape continue to evolve. You will help anticipate what’s ahead, navigate novel and complex regulatory questions, and establish the legal and regulatory foundation that enables CoreWeave to innovate responsibly and grow globally. This is an opportunity to have a meaningful impact on both our products and how we operate at a pivotal stage of growth. If you thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, enjoy solving complex problems, and are eager to make a significant impact, CoreWeave is the place for you. About the role: Reporting to the Senior Director & Lead Managing Counsel, Privacy, Regulatory & Compliance, you will set the legal framework for how products are designed, reviewed, approved, launched, and operated in a rapidly evolving global regulatory environment. You will advise senior leaders and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Privacy, AI, Security, Commercial Legal, Supply Chain, and Global Operations to translate complex requirements into practical decisions and scalable controls.  In this Role You Will: Own and mature CoreWeave’s product regulatory governance program, including product-review processes, approval frameworks, policies, decision records, training, control mappings, and evidence demonstrating compliance. Lead legal review of new and evolving products, features, AI capabilities, data uses, and infrastructure initiatives throughout the product lifecycle; identify requirements, conduct international product regulatory risk assessments, and recommend controls, approvals, and launch conditions. Partner with Product and Engineering to embed privacy by design and default, responsible AI, security, data-governance, transparency, and other requirements into product architecture, roadmaps, and development processes. Advise Supply Chain and Global Operations on product-related regulatory matters, including technology transitions, state packaging requirements, equipment compliance, and scalable supply-chain regulatory programs. Partner with Product Commercial Legal to align product functionality, customer commitments, contracting positions, disclosures, technical documentation, and marketing claims with legal requirements and approved controls. Monitor, interpret, and operationalize U.S. and international product, privacy, AI, data, cybersecurity, consumer-protection, and digital-services laws; advise senior leadership on product roadmaps, market entry, and business models. Lead significant regulatory inquiries, audits, investigations, and policy engagements involving CoreWeave’s products and services; coordinate cross-functional responses, oversee outside counsel, drive remediation, and provide subject-matter leadership across Legal and Compliance. Who You Are: 7+ years of relevant legal experience, including substantial experience counseling complex technology products; a mix of law firm and in-house experience is preferred. Demonstrated ability to serve as the senior legal advisor to Product and Engineering leaders and independently resolve novel, high-impact regulatory issues throughout the product lifecycle. Deep expertise in multiple regulatory areas relevant to AI and cloud products, such as AI governance, privacy and data protection, cybersecurity, consumer protection, data regulation, or digital-services regulation. Strong technical fluency and the ability to translate product functionality, system architecture, data flows, model behavior, and technical documentation into clear legal and engineering actions. Experience designing and leading product governance programs, including review and approval frameworks, policies, controls, training, audit-ready evidence, and monitoring. title: Director of Security Assurance & Trust
description: Joining Collibra’s Field Security team The Field Security team acts as the critical bridge between our Field teams and our customers, ensuring customer trust remains our number one priority. We engage with Sales, Product, and Engineering to structure security initiatives that add business value and foster high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty. Our customers are our true north, and we live this value by consulting directly with strategically important customers to provide resolution on significant, business-critical security issues. This is a hybrid role based in our New York office. Our hybrid model means you’ll work from the office at least two days each week. This setup helps us stay connected, work more closely together, and keep making progress as a team. The Director of Security Assurance & Trust at Collibra are responsible for Strategic Advisor to Sales combining a deep cybersecurity expertise with ability to engage externally with customers, prospects and regulators. Excellent Communicator with ability to articulate and own the security narrative and insights to help drive sales. Customer-Facing Security Leader acting as a public facing persona representing Collibra’s security posture, roadmap and philosophy. Collaborating and negotiating with internal business, product, and functional leadership to define and manage customer requirements, regulations into clear security objectives. Analyzing customer needs, requirements, and expectations from a product technical and security perspective to optimally allocate Field Security resources. Handling complex, strategically important situations by forming and implementing complex project plans, specifications, and schedules to ensure critical outcomes are met. Continually evaluating the security organization’s capability to define, develop, and implement structures and controls that are scalable, resilient, and effective. Engaging the full set of stakeholders to ensure appropriate decision-making regarding security analysis, planning, and evolution. You have Extensive 5 - 7 years professional experience in an information security, field security, or customer-facing technical leadership role. A proven track record of consulting with senior leadership and enterprise customers on business-critical security concerns and structural/operational implications. Strong understanding of compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, EU AI Act, DORA etc.) Excellent written and verbal communications; comfortable presenting to internal and external stakeholders. Demonstrated experience establishing organizational standards and managing complex project plans in a rapidly evolving environment. Deep understanding of multiple security perspectives, including customer business cases, physical infrastructure, and information assurance. Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, particularly working alongside Sales, Product, and Engineering teams. A bachelor’s degree or equivalent related working experience is required. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. You are Analytical, leveraging multiple sources of data to gain a holistic understanding before reaching conclusions and making clear-eyed decisions about field security risks and trade-offs. Authentic, demonstrating self-awareness, self-mastery, and a commitment to ongoing reflection that reinforces integrity across the leadership team. Inclusive, soliciting diverse opinions, giving others time to think, and leading others to recognize the assumptions and biases that might sway decision-making. Adaptable, ensuring a holistic approach to learning and adapting in a rapidly evolving environment. Consistent, demonstrating a consistent approach and manner in all circumstances and ensuring actions align with personal and company values. Measures of success Within your first month, you will gain a holistic understanding of Collibra's field security landscape, establish relationships with key Sales, Product, and Engineering stakeholders, and evaluate our current organizational standards. Within your third month, you will actively consult with senior stakeholders within strategically important customers, addressing their critical issues, and begin setting priorities to direct/re-direct field security efforts. Within your sixth month, you will define and manage the Field Security strategic roadmap, implement scalable controls, and ensure security initiatives actively add business value and foster customer loyalty Compensation for this role The standard base salary range for this position is $224,000.00 - $280,000.00 per year. This position is not eligible for additional commission-based compensation. Salary offers are based on a combination of factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skills, and location. title: Veeam Data Cloud Vault Solution Specialist
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. Join us in driving one of Veeam\'s most strategic initiatives: accelerating customer adoption of Veeam Data Cloud Vault . As a Sales Specialist focused on driving the expansion of Veeam’s fastest growing product through out our channel,  you'll lead crucial conversations that shape the future of data protection. Reporting to the WW Veeam Vault Sales Leader, you'll partner with Account teams, Solution Engineers, and our channel organization to help customers embrace Veeam’s managed storage service and fuel Veeam's continued market leadership. This quota-carrying role leads customer and channel transformation across a defined geographic territory. Working alongside dedicated Solution Engineers and account teams, you'll drive commercial wins by demonstrating the compelling business value of our cloud-native platform. Your tasks will include Execute on territory strategy and pipeline development across a set of priority partners and 500+ strategic accounts to achieve quarterly revenue targets. Collaborate on a daily basis with your territory’s AEs and channel managers to ensure great account-level partnering and channel stratgy; ensure top deals are on track with the right Field + Specialist pursuit team engaged. Provide weekly product-specific forecast updates for your territory. Prepare and lead value-based customer discussions focused on long-term benefits of a wholly managed Veeam solution. Design channel programs to maximizing adoption and revenue impact. Build and maintain strategic relationships across channel and customer organizations to drive continued business growth and install base attach. Identify priority accounts and opportunities to partner with Solution Engineers to deliver compelling technical and business value messaging. Provide market intelligence and customer feedback to identify repeatable sales tactics that increase win rates and help build a “win formula.” Master our competitive positioning, market trends, and pricing strategies to drive exponential growth from territory channel partners What we expect from you 8+ years of enterprise software sales experience, with proven success in cloud/SaaS solutions. Track record of success in and career growth in field sales and channel development with experience working effectively in specialist sales models preferred. Proven capability in Enterprise software sales and SaaS business models, ideally in the data protection, data management or M365 sectors. Exceptional skills in business case development, commercial negotiations, and stakeholder management. Bachelor\'s degree in business or related field (or equivalent experience). Strong team player / coach mentality – expect to be personally engaged in opportunities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Willingness to travel up to 30% of the time. Fluent German, both written and spoken.
